selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What kind of place does the traveler enter at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: He enters a lonely, empty wild area.

questions.question: What keeps him suspended in the well?
questions.answer: A tree growing from the wall catches him in the middle of the descent.

questions.question: Why is his position on the tree temporary rather than stable?
questions.answer: The roots holding it are being worn away, so his support will not last.

questions.question: What do the two rats look like?
questions.answer: One is white and the other is black.

questions.question: What makes the tree remarkable?
questions.answer: One tree bears fruit from many different kinds of trees.

questions.question: What contrast appears between his inner faculties and his lower self?
questions.answer: His inner faculties suffer and sense the seriousness, while his lower self denies it and chases pleasure.

questions.question: Why does the man fail to understand the meaning of what he is seeing?
questions.answer: He is thoughtless and foolish, so he treats it as random and ordinary.

questions.question: Why is that behavior even more misguided than it first appears?
questions.answer: Because some of what he eats is poisonous and adds harm to danger.

questions.question: What broader lesson can be inferred from his story in this passage alone?
questions.answer: A person’s way of thinking can blind him to meaning and increase his suffering.

questions.question: Why is his state described as neither life nor death?
questions.answer: Because he does not escape through death, yet he also does not enjoy real living.

questions.question: What sequence of events leads the man from the open land into the well?
questions.answer: He wanders through a barren place, sees a lion coming at him, runs away, and jumps into a dry well.

questions.question: Which event begins the chain of dangers?
questions.answer: The appearance of a lion begins it.

questions.question: How are the two rats identified?
questions.answer: They are distinguished by color, one white and one black.

questions.question: How close is the dragon to the man’s foot?
questions.answer: Its head comes up to a point about thirty yards below his foot.

questions.question: What is the dragon doing below?
questions.answer: It raises its head toward the man and comes close beneath him.

questions.question: What inward reaction do his heart, spirit, and mind have?
questions.answer: They are in anguish and distress.

questions.question: Which parts of the man are inwardly grieving?
questions.answer: His heart, spirit, and mind are grieving.

questions.question: What inward suffering is taking place that the lower self ignores?
questions.answer: His heart, spirit, and mind are crying out in pain.

questions.question: How is his suffering described in the final lines?
questions.answer: He remains trapped in torment without true living or release through death.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the traveler’s environment besides its being dangerous?
questions.answer: It suggests the scene is full of signs and hidden meanings.

questions.question: Where does he jump in order to get away?
questions.answer: He jumps into a deep dry well.

questions.question: What does he discover when he checks the top of the well?
questions.answer: The lion is still there waiting above.

questions.question: What does the gathering of poisonous creatures around him add to the scene?
questions.answer: It shows that danger is not only above and below him but also all around him.

questions.question: What does he see below him after looking down?
questions.answer: He sees a frightening dragon with its head raised toward him.
